CHAPTER 2  
CONTEXT 
2.1 Introduction 
This chapter will delve into the history of digital learning and theoretical 
foundations of education, while additionally evaluating some of the most 
influential educational platforms for GCSE students and the wider public. Aiming 
to uncover key features and strategies that contribute to effective learning 
outcomes; and finally culminating into an overview of gaps within existing 
research and products. 
2.2 Historical Overview of eLearning 
Electronic learning or eLearning began with the CBT Systems, IT tutorial 
software that used CD-ROMs which would upload to the computer (Cross, 2004). 
In the 1990s with the rise of the internet, companies like Cisco and UNISYS 
began to utilise the capabilities of online content delivery; the platforms became 
more popular during the dot-com boom between the years 1999 and 2000 
(Cross, 2004; Sun, et al., 2014). During the 2000s, the classroom began to use 
eLearning as a supplementary tool, for use at school and at home (Cross, 2004; 
Sun, et al., 2014). 
After the Corona virus pandemic, the “supplementary” mindset shifted to it 
being an essential part of the learning experience, with one universities online 
educational resources going from 2TB to 46TB between March 2019 and March 
2020 (Ebner, et al., 2020). The eLearning market within the UK is valued at 
£7.76bn in 2023 and is expected to have an annual growth rate of 7.49%
